note: Curated fallback lines. {day} is replaced with the day number. Founder reviews before launch.

lines.text: Day 1. A fresh start and a clean slate. Tonight, decide where your phone sleeps, and leave it there.
Day 1. Nothing to prove yet except that you showed up. Check in tonight and that counts as the whole job.
Day 1 is on the wall. Pick the hour that usually gets loud and plan something for it.
Day {day}. You've done this {day} days running. Do today the same way, one evening at a time.
Day {day}. The early days are mostly habit and timing. Notice when the urge tends to show up and be ready then.
Day {day}. Keep it plain today: eat properly, get outside once, and go to bed at a sensible hour.
Day {day}. If a rough moment comes, it passes in a few minutes. Start a round and let the clock carry it.
Day {day}. Boredom tends to arrive around now. Have one three-minute plan ready before the evening starts.
Day 7. The first plate goes on the wall today. Handle tonight the way you handled the last six.
Day 7. One full week. Nothing dramatic, just seven evenings handled. Do the eighth the same way.
Day {day}. You've handled {day} evenings like this one. Handle tonight the same way.
Day {day}. The routine is starting to hold. Keep the phone out of the bedroom and keep checking in.
Day {day}. Look at what set you off in week one and move one thing out of the way tonight.
Day {day}. Steady beats intense. A short walk after dinner is a good way to close the day.
Day {day}. You don't need a big day. You need an ordinary one with a check-in at the end.
Day 14. Halfway. The tally on the wall is yours whatever happens next. Keep the evenings simple.
Day 14. Two weeks done. Your log shows what sets you off, so plan around the worst hour tonight.
Day {day}. Past halfway. The days look alike now, and that is the point. Check in and rest.
Day {day}. When an urge shows up, name it, start a round, and let three minutes go by.
Day {day}. Same plan as yesterday: phone out of the bedroom, lights out at a decent hour, check in.
Day {day}. You've got a routine now. Protect it from late nights, because that is where it gets tested.
Day 21. Three plates on the wall. Now the routine does most of the work. Let it.
Day 21. Three weeks. Keep doing the small things that got you here, starting with an early night.
Day {day}. The finish is in sight, but today is still just today. Handle this evening and check in.
Day {day}. Close to the bell. Don't change what works. Same routine, same check-in, same time.
Day {day}. A few days left. If tonight gets loud, go a round first and decide after.
Day {day}. You know your hard hour by now. Be somewhere else, doing something else, when it comes.
Day {day}. You went the distance. The record stays on the wall. Decide calmly what comes next.
Day {day}. The tally is full. Take a quiet minute to notice what changed in your days, then rest.
Day {day}. You kept going past the bell. Keep the routine that helped and drop the ones that didn't.
Day 1. Every record begins with a single mark. Make today's mark and leave tomorrow for tomorrow.
Day 1. You cannot finish thirty days today. You can finish this one. That is enough.
Day 1. Begin without fuss. The first step is small, and it is also the one that matters most.
Day {day}. The urge wants your attention. Give it three minutes and nothing more.
Day {day}. You control where you put your attention. Put it somewhere useful this evening.
Day {day}. A craving is a visitor, not a resident. Let it knock, and keep doing what you were doing.
Day {day}. Discomfort is information, not an order. Notice it, breathe, and carry on with your evening.
Day {day}. Do the next right thing, then the one after that. A day is only a chain of small choices.
Day 7. Seven days. Not a triumph, just evidence. You can do what you said you would do.
Day 7. A week of choices made one at a time. Make the next one the same way.
Day {day}. What you practice grows stronger. You have practiced holding the line for {day} days.
Day {day}. The urge rises and falls whether you act on it or not. Wait for the fall.
Day {day}. Most of discipline is arranging the room before the moment arrives. Arrange tonight's room now.
Day {day}. You don't have to feel ready. You only have to stay with the plan for the next hour.
Day {day}. Today asks for nothing heroic. Keep your word to yourself in small, quiet ways.
Day 14. Halfway is a place to stand, not a place to rest. Stand here and look ahead.
Day 14. Two weeks of practice. The road ahead is the same road. Walk it the same way.
Day {day}. Calm is a skill, and you have been training it. Use it when the evening gets loud.
Day {day}. The mind makes the urge seem permanent. It never is. Three minutes will show you.
Day {day}. You cannot choose every thought. You can choose the next thing your hands do.
Day {day}. Keep your attention on what is in front of you. Tonight, that is one evening.
Day 21. Three weeks. What once took effort now takes less. Notice that, and keep going.
Day 21. A habit is built by repetition and kept by attention. Keep paying attention tonight.
Day {day}. The end of a thing is like the start: one day, handled well. Handle this one.
Day {day}. Don't count the days left. Make this day count, and the rest will follow.
Day {day}. The last stretch tests patience more than will. Be patient with the hour you are in.
Day {day}. You have kept your word for {day} days. Keep it once more, quietly, tonight.
Day {day}. The record is written. What you learned about yourself is yours to keep.
Day {day}. The bell has rung. Rest, then choose deliberately whether to go again.
Day {day}. You did what you set out to do, one day at a time. That method still works.
Day 1. Fresh start. Tonight, put your phone on charge outside the bedroom. That's the whole game plan.
Day 1. Tell one friend you're doing this, then check in before bed. Two jobs, both small.
Day 1. Write down your riskiest hour of the day and plan three minutes for it. Start there.
Day {day}. Phone out of the bedroom tonight. That's the game plan.
Day {day}. Get outside for ten minutes before dinner. Fresh air beats a long evening on the couch.
Day {day}. If the urge hits, tap Go a round before you think about anything else. Then decide.
Day {day}. Set a bedtime and stick to it. Late nights are where most rounds get hard.
Day {day}. Make an if-then plan: if you're bored after nine, then you go for a walk.
Day 7. First plate. Text your camp a thumbs-up, then do exactly what you did yesterday.
Day 7. One week down. Look at your log and cut out the one thing that keeps showing up.
Day {day}. Do twenty squats right now. Then check in. Short, simple, done.
Day {day}. Plan tonight before it starts: what you'll do at nine, at ten, and when the lights go out.
Day {day}. Get your phone off the pillow. Charge it across the room and get up to turn off the alarm.
Day {day}. Cook something tonight. Busy hands, a full stomach, and an early night.
Day {day}. If you're scrolling with no reason, stop, stand up, and go a round instead.
Day 14. Halfway. Check your log, find your worst hour, and have a plan ready before it arrives.
Day 14. Two weeks in. Message one person in your camp and ask how they're holding up.
Day {day}. Lights out by eleven. Set an alarm for the time you start winding down.
Day {day}. Take a walk without your phone today. Twenty minutes, then back to normal.
Day {day}. When it gets loud, don't negotiate. Go a round first and talk to yourself after.
Day {day}. Plan something for Saturday night now, so it doesn't plan itself for you.
Day 21. Three plates. Keep the routine exactly as it is. Don't loosen the bedtime now.
Day 21. Write down the two things that helped most. Keep doing both this week.
Day {day}. Close to the bell. Same routine tonight: phone out, lights off, check in.
Day {day}. If you feel restless, get up and move for five minutes before you do anything else.
Day {day}. Keep your hardest hour busy. Book something into it today, even a phone call.
Day {day}. Check in early tonight, then put the phone away and leave it there.
Day {day}. You went the distance. Write down what worked, then decide whether to go again.
Day {day}. Record's on the wall. Keep the bedtime and the phone rule; they earned their place.
Day {day}. You're past the bell. Pick one habit from this month and keep it for the next.
Day 1. Clean slate, new clock, zero drama. The only thing on today's list is showing up tonight.
Day 1. The clock's running and it has no opinions. Check in tonight and it stays that way.
Day 1. Every tally wall starts empty. Yours gets its first stroke tonight. Try not to make it a big deal.
Day {day}. One more and the tally gets more interesting. Don't stop at the bell.
Day {day}. Boredom is a terrible sparring partner with great timing. Have a plan for when it shows up.
Day {day}. Your phone would like to stay up late with you. Tell it you have an early start.
Day {day}. The urge keeps showing up uninvited. Give it three minutes in the waiting room and it leaves.
Day {day}. Nothing heroic needed today. Just the usual: check in, sleep, repeat. Thrilling stuff.
Day 7. A whole week, and the wall finally has some brass on it. Try to look unimpressed.
Day 7. Seven strokes and a plate. Your camp will notice. Act like you do this every week.
Day {day}. One more and you're in double digits. Don't stop at the bell.
Day {day}. The bag isn't going to swing itself. Actually it is, it's in the app. Go breathe with it.
Day {day}. Your evening has two settings: plan or autopilot. Autopilot has terrible taste in timing.
Day {day}. Double digits suit you. Keep the phone out of the bedroom and keep the streak boring.
Day {day}. You've lasted every round so far. The next one is three minutes, which is shorter than most ads.
Day 14. Halfway. The tally wall is starting to look like someone means business. That someone is you.
Day 14. Two weeks. The clock is unbothered, and frankly, so are you. Keep it that way tonight.
Day {day}. The late-night scroll is calling. Let it go to voicemail and go to bed.
Day {day}. You and the clock have an understanding now. Don't make it awkward at eleven tonight.
Day {day}. The urge is like a loud neighbor. Annoying, temporary, and gone by the time you've made tea.
Day {day}. Past halfway and still checking in. The wall is running out of empty space, in a good way.
Day 21. Three plates on the wall. At this point the routine is basically running itself. Let it drive.
Day 21. Three weeks. If anyone asks what changed, tell them you got very good at going to bed.
Day {day}. Close enough to see the bell, far enough to stay sharp. Keep your guard up tonight.
Day {day}. The final stretch. The clock doesn't do speeches, so just check in and get some sleep.
Day {day}. You've survived every evening so far. This one has the same plot. You know the ending.
Day {day}. The tally wall is nearly full. Leave room for the belt and keep the evening quiet.
Day {day}. You went the distance. The wall is full, the belt is up, and the clock is still unbothered.
Day {day}. Thirty strokes and a belt. Take a bow, then go to bed at a reasonable hour.
Day {day}. Past the bell and still going. The clock respects that, in its own quiet way.
